h1: The 8 Best Glass Desktop Whiteboards of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Glass Desktop Whiteboards: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight glass desktop whiteboards from Quartet and others, compared on size, storage and keyboard-stand design.
summary: The Quartet GDP1723W is our top pick for people who want a big magnetic glass panel on the desk. The TSJ OFFICE board is the best two-in-one because it doubles as a keyboard stand with a drawer. For a first glass board on a tiny budget, the 8 by 6 inch mini with five markers is the cheapest way in.
intro: The mistake most people make with a desktop whiteboard is buying the smallest one and then finding it holds a single to-do list. Writing area, not the frame, is what you are really buying, so size deserves more attention than finish.

We reviewed eight glass boards and ranked them on writing area, storage, the accessories that come in the box, and how much desk each one takes. Boards that double as keyboard stands are scored differently from flat pads, and we say so where it matters.

products.name: Quartet Glass Whiteboard Desktop Panel, Magnetic, 17"x23", Dry Erase, with Accessory Trays and Magnets (GDP1723W)
products.verdict: The largest writing area here, with magnets and trays to match.
products.description:
The Quartet GDP1723W is a 17 by 23 inch glass desktop panel with a magnetic surface. It comes with magnets and accessory trays, and the listing says one marker is included.

It wins because it offers the biggest writing area in the group, the only magnetic surface with trays, and a known brand. The tradeoff against everything below it is price, as it is the only board in the $100 to $200 bucket, and it takes far more desk than the small pads.

Buy it if the board is a working tool for planning rather than a notepad. The caveat is footprint: measure your desk before ordering.
products.idealFor: Planners who want a full-size glass board beside the monitor.
products.skipIf: Your desk has little spare room.

products.name: TSJ OFFICE Small Desktop Whiteboard, Glass Dry Erase Board, Computer Keyboard Stand with Drawer
products.verdict: A keyboard stand, drawer and whiteboard in one footprint.
products.description:
The TSJ OFFICE board has a glass dry erase surface, a built-in storage drawer, and doubles as a keyboard stand. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket.

It ranks second because it gets two jobs out of one piece of desk. Compared with the Quartet above it has no magnetic surface or trays, but it costs far less and hides small items in the drawer.

It suits crowded desks where every inch counts. The caveat is that the listing gives no board dimensions in our data, so check the writing area on the product page.
products.idealFor: Small desks that need storage and a board.
products.skipIf: You want a large writing area.

products.name: Quartet Glass Dry Erase White Board, Desktop Computer Pad for Notetaking, 18"x6" with Storage (GDP186)
products.verdict: A wide, shallow strip that fits in front of a monitor.
products.description:
The Quartet GDP186 is an 18 by 6 inch glass writing pad with storage and one dry erase marker included. It is priced in the $25 to $50 bucket.

It lands third because the shallow shape suits notes and reminders but not diagrams. Against the TSJ above it gives up the keyboard-stand function, and against the pads below it offers a wider surface.

It is a good fit for quick notes and lists. The caveat is height: six inches runs out fast.
products.idealFor: Notes and lists in front of a monitor.

products.name: Small Glass Desktop Whiteboard Dry Erase Board with Calculator, Keyboard Stand Organizer
products.verdict: A keyboard-stand board with a calculator built in.
products.description:
This small glass whiteboard includes a calculator and works as a keyboard stand organizer. The listing says markers and an eraser come with it, and it sits in the $25 to $50 bucket.

It ranks below the TSJ because the calculator is the main extra rather than a storage drawer. For number-heavy desk work that is a fair swap.

Choose it if you add up figures all day. The caveat is that the board dimensions are not given in our data.
products.idealFor: Desk workers who do quick sums.
products.skipIf: You want storage over a calculator.

products.name: Quartet Dry Erase White Board 9"W x 11"H Desktop Glass Pad with Removable Clip and Marker (GDE119)
products.verdict: A letter-sized glass pad with a clip for paper.
products.description:
The Quartet GDE119 is a 9 by 11 inch glass writing pad with a removable paper clip and a marker. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket.

It ranks fifth because it is a plain pad with no storage or stand. The removable clip is its distinctive touch, letting you hold a printed reference beside your notes.

It suits people who want a simple, familiar-brand pad. The caveat is that it has no extras beyond the clip.
products.idealFor: A simple pad for daily notes.

products.name: Small Desktop Glass Whiteboard Dry-Erase Board, Computer Keyboard Stand with Drawer
products.verdict: Same keyboard-stand-with-drawer idea, with a grey finish option.
products.description:
This small glass board is a keyboard stand with a built-in drawer and a glass dry erase surface, with a grey finish option. It is in the $25 to $50 bucket.

It ranks below the TSJ OFFICE because it offers the same format without the same brand recognition. The grey option is the one real differentiator.

Pick it if the finish matters to your desk. The caveat is thin listing detail, including no stated writing size.
products.idealFor: Buyers matching a grey desk setup.

products.name: Desktop Black Glass Dry Erase Whiteboard with Reversible Wood Stand, Small (9.5"x6.7")
products.verdict: A tiny black glass board on a reversible wood stand.
products.description:
This is a 9.5 by 6.7 inch black glass dry erase board with a reversible wood stand. A marker and eraser come with it, and it sits in the under $25 bucket.

It ranks seventh because the writing area is small. It beats the mini below on stand design and size, but it is not meant for more than a list.

It suits a minimalist desk. The caveat is that the small size limits what you can write.

products.name: Black Mini Desktop Pure Glass Whiteboard, Small Glass Dry-Erase Whiteboard, 8"x6" with 5 markers
products.verdict: The cheapest way to try a glass board, with five markers.
products.description:
This black mini board is 8 by 6 inches of pure glass with five markers included per the listing. It carries the lowest price in the guide, in the under $25 bucket.

It ranks last because it is the smallest surface and has no stand or storage. What it offers is the lowest cost of entry and a generous marker count.

Buy it as a low-risk first glass board. The caveat is size: 8 by 6 inches fills quickly.

whatMatters.detail: This is the usable glass surface in inches. It decides whether the board holds a list or a plan. Look for the exact dimensions in the title and bullet points, not just words like small or large.

Some boards double as a stand that lifts the keyboard and adds a surface. That saves desk space but ties the board to your keyboard position. Check the listing for the words keyboard stand and confirm your keyboard fits.
A magnetic glass board lets you pin notes with magnets. Only the Quartet GDP1723W lists magnets here. If you pin reminders, look for the word magnetic and confirm magnets are included.
A drawer or tray keeps markers and clips from spreading across the desk. It matters on small desks. Check whether storage is built in or sold separately.
A board with no marker is unusable on arrival. Counts range from one to five on these listings. Confirm what the listing says is in the box.

faq.a: Several do. The mini lists five, the GDE119 and GDP186 list one each, and the GDP1723W lists one per the listing. Check the box contents before buying.

faq.q: Is glass better than a plastic board?
faq.a: Glass is generally smoother to wipe. The listings here describe glass surfaces, but they do not give ghosting data, so rely on the surface description alone.

faq.q: Will a keyboard-stand board fit my keyboard?
faq.a: The listings do not give full dimensions in our data. Measure your keyboard and compare to the dimensions on the product page.

faq.q: Is a black glass board harder to use?
faq.a: The two black boards come with markers or an eraser per their listings. Confirm which marker type each expects before you buy.

faq.q: Is the 17 by 23 inch Quartet worth it?
faq.a: If you plan on the desk, yes. It is the only magnetic board with trays here, but it is also the only one in the $100 to $200 bucket.

faq.q: How do I clean a glass board?
faq.a: Follow the manufacturer's instructions. The listings do not state a method, so check the product page.

finalTake: The Quartet GDP1723W is the best glass desktop board if you have the space. The TSJ OFFICE is the smarter choice for small desks, and the 8 by 6 inch mini is the cheap way in. Match the writing area to how you actually use the board.
